en.name: Portfolio Board
en.subtitle: Offline spec and stage board
en.short_description: Browse 33 bundled project specs offline and track the stage each one is at.
en.description:
Portfolio Board is an offline reader and stage tracker for the American Group LLC project portfolio: 28 candidate projects and 5 shared-infrastructure specs, with all 198 of their specification documents bundled inside the app.

The Portfolio tab groups every record into the categories the roadmap defines, shows the stage spread as a bar, and lets you tap a stage to see exactly which records sit in it. Browse searches every word of all 198 documents, counts the matches per document, shows a verbatim snippet, and opens that document with the term highlighted. Results can be narrowed by category, stage, priority tier (T1 to T4), spec depth and record kind.

Health is the portfolio summary: where records stand now against where the source documents put them, the Tier-1 greenlight gate rollup (criteria met, LOIs signed, gates cleared), the count of full, thin and stub specs together with the measured rule behind those labels, category coverage thinnest first, and which records have gone longest untouched.

Each project opens on a tracking tab plus one tab per document - README, DESIGN, ARCHITECTURE, ROADMAP, COMPETITIVE and GO-TO-MARKET, or INTEGRATION for shared infrastructure. The tracking tab carries the project's portfolio-table facts, its ten-axis priority score axis by axis, its greenlight gate criteria, an index of its documents, and its stage history. Moving a project between stages takes a bottom sheet and an optional note explaining why.

Documents render as markdown with real tables, so competitor matrices and score grids stay readable. Mermaid and ASCII diagrams are shown as labelled source rather than redrawn as pictures the app cannot honestly draw.

What it does not do. Everything shown comes from one snapshot of the roadmap tree compiled into the build, so there is no network, no sync, no account and no sign-in. You cannot add projects or edit the specifications; the set of records is fixed until a new build ships. Stage moves and their notes are stored on your device only, are never written back to the documents, and can be cleared from Settings to return the board to what the documents say. The screens and the bundled documents are in English.
en.promotional_text: Every roadmap document for 33 portfolio records, bundled offline: full-text search, spec-depth and gate health, and a stage board you keep on your device.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing Portfolio Board.

Portfolio Board is an offline reader and stage tracker for a fixed set of product specification documents. No account, no sign-in, no demo credentials and no in-app purchase: it opens straight onto the Portfolio tab.

Everything it displays ships inside the binary. A single ~1 MB asset, assets/roadmap/portfolio.json, holds 33 project records across 7 categories and the 198 specification documents behind them; lib/services/roadmap_repository.dart reads it from the bundle and there is no network implementation at all. The app therefore behaves identically in airplane mode. There are no refresh spinners, no "offline" errors and no sync, because no request is ever made - please do not read that as a broken feed.

Test instructions:
1. Launch. The Portfolio tab lists every record grouped by category (Vertical AI SaaS, Sales & Marketing, Developer & Infrastructure, Workflow & Productivity, Cybersecurity, Finance, Shared infrastructure) with the stage each one is at.
2. Tap any record to open its project page, then tap a document to read the full specification. Documents are rendered from markdown held in that asset.
3. Browse tab: full-text search across all 198 documents. Search something generic like "pricing"; tapping a result opens the document with the term highlighted where it was found.
4. Health tab: counts by stage, how much content each record actually has, category coverage, and how long each record has gone untouched - all computed on-device in lib/services/portfolio_health.dart.
5. From a project page, open the stage sheet and move a record to a different stage. The move is stored locally as an override; the bundled documents are never rewritten, so the app can always show both what the document says and what you changed.
6. Settings lists what is bundled in this build, the local history of stage moves, and "Reset to the source documents", which discards every override.

Privacy:
• Data collected: nothing. There is no account, no sign-up and no profile. The only thing written is your own stage overrides and their history, stored on the device with shared_preferences.
• Network: none. The app makes no requests. The single exception is that tapping an external http link inside a document hands that URL to the system browser.
• Tracking: none. There is no advertising or analytics SDK; the advertising identifier is not read and no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears. A Firebase Crashlytics bootstrap is present but inactive - no Firebase configuration file is included.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.

_blocked.no_copy_drafted: Should probably not be published at all.
_blocked.evidence: lib/services/roadmap_repository.dart loads assets/roadmap/portfolio.json from the bundle and states there is deliberately no network implementation because 'the specs live in the repository'. The UI is AGL's own delivery tracker — stages, gate criteria, portfolio health, 30-day plans, per-project documents. It has no value to a member of the public and it publishes internal roadmap data.
_blocked.to_unblock: A decision: distribute internally (TestFlight / Play internal testing) and drop the public listing, or confirm the bundled roadmap contains nothing confidential.
